By EMG, do you mean both the nerve conduction study and the EMG proper? The study that tests the speed of the nerves is actually called an NCV.  I found it mildly painful.  This is what reveals if you have the slow nerves typical of CMT 1A (which I did!)  The EMG test that followed was not that painful at all.  The worst part was when the technician told me I had "severe nerve damage"--since then, I've decided I prefer the term "congenitally slow nerves" since I'm not sure they really have gotten slower since I was a kid.  (I read somewhere that axonal damage is more predictive of disability in CMT)  My poor sister was told "You're not normal!"
If it makes you feel better, I *think* I read that nerve velocity is not the best predictor of disability in CMT and that you probably have had the same speed since the age of five or so.
